question.questionText: I think the exam will be very difficult and you are not studying at all.

choices.text: You are not going to fail the exam.
choices.raw: A. You are not going to fail the exam.

choices.text: You are not passing the exam.
choices.raw: B. You are not passing the exam.

choices.text: You are not going to pass the exam.
choices.raw: C. You are not going to pass the exam.

question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The sentence 'I think the exam will be very difficult and you are not studying at all.' suggests that the speaker believes the listener will not succeed in the exam because they are not preparing. The correct answer should express a prediction about the future, specifically about not passing the exam. The structure 'be going to + verb' is used to talk about something that is likely to happen in the future based on present evidence.
  • A. You are not going to fail the exam. (sentence): 'Not going to fail' means the person will pass the exam, which is the opposite of the speaker's prediction.
  • B. You are not passing the exam. (sentence): 'Are not passing' uses the present continuous tense, which is not appropriate for making a future prediction based on current evidence.
  • C. You are not going to pass the exam. (sentence): 'Not going to pass' correctly uses the 'be going to' future form to predict that the person will fail the exam.
Related structure or vocabulary: be going to + verb: used to express a prediction about the future based on present evidence.
